items.question: A Messages API response comes back with stop_reason "tool_use". What should your code do next?
choices: Run the requested tool(s), send the results back as tool_result blocks in a new user message, and call the API again
Show the response to the user; the turn is finished
Retry the same request, because the output was cut off
Raise an error, because the model refused
items.explanation: tool_use means Claude is asking for a tool call. Your loop executes it and returns a tool_result matched by tool_use_id, repeating until stop_reason is end_turn.

items.question: stop_reason is "max_tokens". What happened?
choices: A stop sequence you provided was generated
The output hit the max_tokens limit you set and is probably truncated
The model finished its answer naturally
The prompt exceeded the context window
items.explanation: max_tokens means generation was cut off at your limit. Raise the limit or continue the response. A natural finish is end_turn, and a matched stop sequence is stop_sequence.

items.question: What does prompt caching save you?
choices: Rate-limit errors, because cached requests skip the API
Cost and latency on a repeated, identical prompt prefix (e.g. a long system prompt or document), because cached reads are billed far below normal input
Output tokens, because responses are reused for identical questions
items.explanation: Caching stores the processed prefix up to a cache_control breakpoint. Later requests with the exact same prefix read it cheaply and faster. Responses are never cached, and any change before the breakpoint misses the cache.

items.question: When is the Message Batches API the right call?
choices: A chat UI that needs streaming tokens
An agent loop where each step depends on the previous tool result
Large, non-urgent jobs (nightly classification, eval runs, backfills) where about 50% lower cost matters more than latency
items.explanation: Batches are asynchronous, at about half the cost, with results within 24 hours (often much sooner). Interactive or step-dependent work belongs on the regular Messages API.

items.question: Your system prompt starts with today's timestamp, followed by a 20k-token policy document marked for caching. Why is the cache hit rate near zero?
choices: The cache matches on an exact prefix, and the timestamp changes it on every request; move variable content after the cached block
Caching only works on user messages
Documents over 10k tokens can't be cached
Cache hits require streaming to be enabled
items.explanation: Put stable content first (tools, system, long documents) and per-request content last. Anything that changes before the breakpoint invalidates the cached prefix.
